The upper part has a carboxylic acid fragment: the carboxyl carbon forms a double bond with the upper oxygen and is connected to OH on the right; on the left there is an α-carbon connected to R, the carboxyl carbon, and HN. HN is further connected to the central carbon in the middle. The middle central carbon is also connected to the right oxygen and the lower oxygen. The curved arrows in the figure indicate electron movement and are not counted as chemical bonds; bonds involving hydrogen are not counted. Reasoning: count non-hydrogen bonds by the specified regions. Upper fragment: α-C–carboxyl C is 1, carboxyl C=O double bond counts as 2, carboxyl C–O is 1, α-C–N is 1, N–central C is 1, totaling 6. Central/lower fragment: central C–right O is 1, central C–lower O is 1, lower O–acyl C is 1, acyl C=O double bond counts as 2, acyl C–lower carbon is 1, totaling 6. The total is 6 + 6 = 12.
